title: First Trimester Nutrition Checklist: Folate, Iron, and Safer Foods
excerpt: Prioritize folic acid, iron-rich foods, hydration, and cooked foods during weeks 1–12
content:
## Introduction to First Trimester Nutrition

During the first trimester, nutrition plays a crucial role in fetal development. Providing adequate nutrients helps the fetus develop fully and reduces the risk of birth defects. In this article, we will explore the essential factors in first trimester nutrition, including folate, iron, and safer foods.

## Folate: A Crucial Nutrient

Folate is a vital nutrient during pregnancy, helping prevent neural tube defects in the fetus. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), pregnant women should take 400 micrograms of folate daily. Folate can be found in foods like leafy greens, fruits, and dairy products.

## Iron: An Essential Nutrient

Iron is an essential nutrient during pregnancy, helping produce red blood cells and provide oxygen to the fetus. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), pregnant women should take 27 milligrams of iron daily. Iron can be found in foods like red meat, poultry, fish, and legumes.

## Safer Foods

During the first trimester, pregnant women should avoid foods with a high risk of containing bacteria, viruses, and parasites. According to the National Health Service (NHS), foods to avoid include:

* Raw or undercooked foods
* Foods containing Listeria bacteria
* Foods containing Norovirus
* Foods containing Toxoplasma parasites

## Foods to Prioritize

During the first trimester, pregnant women should prioritize nutrient-rich foods, including:

* Leafy greens and fruits
* Dairy products
* Red meat, poultry, fish, and legumes
* Whole grains and starchy foods

## Cooking Foods Safely

To ensure food safety, pregnant women should cook foods thoroughly before eating. According to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), foods should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 74°C to kill bacteria and viruses.

## Conclusion

Nutrition during the first trimester plays a vital role in fetal development. Providing adequate nutrients, including folate, iron, and safer foods, helps the fetus develop fully and reduces the risk of birth defects. Pregnant women should consult a [meal planner](/planner) to have a suitable and safe nutrition plan.

## When to Seek Help

If you have any questions or concerns about nutrition during pregnancy, consult your doctor or a registered dietitian. You can also find information on our [website](/blog/topics) to learn more about nutrition and health during pregnancy.
